newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran paper calls for revamp of tax system.
newsitem.headline: Iran paper calls for revamp of tax system.

text.p: An Iranian newspaper on Tuesday called on parliament to revamp the country's tax system which was pushing government employees below the poverty line.

"In the first instance the Majlis (parliament) deputies should make sure whether the budget bill provides for a sound tax system with enough revenues from the income of the privileged," the English-language Tehran Times said in an editorial "opinion" column.

"Following the reform programmes launched by President (Akbar Hashemi) Rafsanjani, the private sector earns income with astronomical figures because the tax system has not been proportionately revamped," it said.
Parliament is discussing the government's proposed $108 billion budget for the next Iranian year beginning on March 21.
While Iranian state employees were being hit hard by the taxation system, businessmen were growing richer because of rising prices, Tehran Times said.
"Most of the government employees live below the poverty line. And some of them have to work on more than one shift to be able to meet the cost of an ordinary life."
"However, the businessmen do not face any financial problems but enjoy the bonanza of rising prices every year," the daily paper reported.
Under the proposed budget for the next Iranian year, revenue from taxation is expected to reach 18.7 trillon rials ($10.7 billion) or 25 percent of government revenue.
